task.description: WF-02 Step 1b hard gate. Read lib/letflow/design/req059-pin-resolver.md directly and independently. Verify every PIN-01..04 acceptance criterion is covered, unambiguous, and contains zero implementation code. Independently resolve the design's own six §9 open questions against the requirement text and shipped code (lib/letflow/engine.ex, lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex, lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_plan.ex) rather than relaying the designer's uncertainty. Specifically verify the claimed engine.ex start_instance/5 reordering (create_snapshot/3 before activate/3, before any pin code could run) against the actual shipped code.
acceptance_criteria: PIN-01 AC1-5 each map to a concrete design element (enumeration/resolution, zero-partial-write ordering, variable_schema violation shape, deterministic ordering)
PIN-02 AC2-4 covered (transactional append, event-log-as-record-of-record, exactly-one variable_schema entry)
PIN-03 AC1/AC2/AC5 covered (PinMissing no-fallback accessor, in-flight isolation from catalog changes)
PIN-04 AC1-5 covered (replay-only effective-pin derivation, child inheritance with conflict recording, API scope boundary)
moduledoc SCOPE GAP requirement (service_catalog/PLC-01, ISS-0672/GH-306 precedent) is stated
No implementation code (function bodies) present anywhere in the design doc -- signatures/@spec/type shapes only
The six §9 open questions are independently resolved (confirmed defensible or flagged as blocking gaps), not just relayed

result.summary: Read lib/letflow/design/req059-pin-resolver.md in full, independently (not the designer's handoff summary), plus REQ-059's requirement text/acceptance_criteria in docs/requirements.yaml and the three cited shipped modules in full. BLOCKING FAIL, one check, no partial credit per WF-02 Step 1b: check (e), 'no implementation code present', fails. Section 3's `start_instance/5` block (lines 154-166) is not a signature or pseudocode-by-function-name as the designer's own handoff claims ('the exact ... reordering ... by function name, not by body') -- it is a complete, real `defp start_instance(...) do ... with {:ok, graph} <- build_graph(...), ... do persist(...) end end` function body with actual match patterns, real argument threading and real control flow, directly copy-pasteable by ELIXIR-DEV. `grep -n '^  def \|^  defp '` on the file confirms this is the only such match and it is exactly this block; the sibling `defmodule Letflow.Engine.PinResolver.Lookup do ... end` block (line 218) is a bare `defstruct`/`@enforce_keys` field-list (permitted -- schema/type shape, no logic), which is the correct precedent this design departs from at line 154. Per .claude/agents/code-designer.md ('no function bodies, no actual .ex/.exs code blocks... CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR will FAIL a design that contains real implementation code') and WF-02 Step 1b check (e), this is disqualifying regardless of how useful the reordering spec is. FAILING ON THIS ALONE, no partial credit -- but recording full findings below since this goes back to CODE-DESIGNER for one rework pass covering everything at once. Everything else independently verified: (1) The reordering claim itself is TRUE, not a false premise -- read engine.ex:367-384 directly: start_instance/5 today runs create_snapshot/3 (a real Repo write via SnapshotStore.create) BEFORE activate/3, so AC2's 'zero rows including instance_definition_snapshots on failed resolution' is genuinely unmet by the current order and the design's reordering (pin resolution moved before create_snapshot/3) is a real, necessary, correctly-scoped fix, not an invented problem. persist/8's current arity (engine.ex:552-561) and append_instance_started_event/6 (engine.ex:766-773) both match the design's arithmetic (persist/10 = +pins +conflicts; append_instance_started_event/8 = +pins +conflicts) -- verified by direct read, not assumed. (2) JsonSchema.validate/2 vs Registry.validate_payload/3 distinction (section 5, section 1) confirmed correct by direct read of both functions' signatures in event_store/registry.ex and registry/json_schema.ex. (3) ServiceScopeValidator.Lookup precedent (section 1, section 4) confirmed -- it is a real 2-field injectable Lookup struct at lib/letflow/definitions/service_scope_validator.ex:105, matching the design's claim that PinResolver.Lookup mirrors it with a third field. (4) PromotionPlan's (SERVICE_TASK,service_id)/(SUB_PROCESS,module_ref) node-attribute convention (section 1, section 4.1) confirmed correct by direct read of promotion_plan.ex:229-244's diff_node_attribute calls. All 8 requirements.yaml acceptance_criteria and the PIN-01..04 sub-AC citations embedded in the requirement's own description text map to a named section (self-check table in section 10) -- independently spot-checked, not just trusted: PIN-01 AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5 -> sections 3/5/4.3; PIN-01 AC2 (module_ref-against-PLC-01 resolution) is correctly named as out-of-scope in the SCOPE GAP rather than silently dropped; PIN-02 AC2/AC3/AC4 -> sections 3/2/4.2; PIN-03 AC1/AC5 -> section 11's pin_for/3; PIN-03 AC2 (mid-flight catalog changes don't affect in-flight instances) is satisfied by construction (no code path anywhere ever re-reads a catalog after resolve/4 returns -- section 6/11 state this as an architectural invariant, which is adequate coverage even without the literal phrase 'mid-flight'); PIN-04 AC1-5 -> sections 6/7/2.6, with AC4 (the GET .../pins route) correctly scoped to S4 while still exposing source_event_id now. GAP NOTED (non-blocking on its own, but should be closed in the same rework pass): the requirement's own PIN-03 AC4 text ('leave a named hook rather than a partial DLQ' for an exhausted PinMissing retry budget) has zero corresponding design element anywhere in the doc -- grepped for 'hook'/'retry budget'/'DLQ', zero matches. This is an omission, not a resolved-and-flagged open question; CODE-DESIGNER should add a named extension point (matching the gateway-stub pattern already used correctly elsewhere in this codebase, e.g. REQ-044's dispatch_exclusive_gateway/4 stub) or explicitly state in the SCOPE GAP why it's deferred, the same way PIN-01 AC1/AC2 and PIN-03 AC3 already are. INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED, the six section-9 open questions (not merely relayed): OQ-1 (R-Co unreachable, :override mechanism inferred) -- accepted as defensible; the design states a concrete, fully-specified override algorithm (section 4.1) rather than leaving it a TBD, which is the correct response to an unreachable source, not a blocking gap. OQ-2 ('most recent' vs 'all' INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND folding) -- design's choice (fold ALL rebind events) is objectively correct given REQ-060's delta-only per-event payload shape is already fixed in the requirement text (folding only the literal 'most recent' event would silently lose earlier rebinds of other refs) -- confirmed correct, not blocking, requirement text's 'most recent' phrasing should be read as loosely worded rather than the design being wrong. OQ-3 (attrs vs opts placement) -- stylistic API-shape choice with no correctness impact either way; not blocking. OQ-4 (parent_instance_id key name, forward guess vs unmerged REQ-062) -- acceptable: this requirement's own scope is the machinery, not REQ-062's call site, and the design correctly flags reconciliation as REQ-062's or a later merge's job rather than guessing silently; not blocking. OQ-5 (variable_schema_lookup totality) -- design's choice (total lookup, no {:error,_} case) is the only reading consistent with PIN-02 AC4's 'still records exactly one variable_schema entry... unconditionally' wording; confirmed correct, not blocking. OQ-6 (override-vs-inheritance collision, inheritance wins even over an override) -- this is the literal, unambiguous reading of PIN-04 AC3's 'inheritance wins' with no stated override exception anywhere in the requirement text; confirmed correct, not blocking. None of the six open questions rises to a blocking gap on its own merits -- each is a stated, reasoned, implementable decision, not a silent guess or a TBD.

issues.description: lib/letflow/design/req059-pin-resolver.md section 3 (lines 154-166) contains a complete real Elixir function body for start_instance/5 (a `with`-chain with real match patterns and control flow), not a signature/type shape -- violates .claude/agents/code-designer.md's 'no implementation code' rule and WF-02 Step 1b check (e). Replace with a numbered/prose call-sequence spec (function names and the order they run in, plus each step's success/failure contract) instead of a literal function body.

The requirement's PIN-03 AC4 text ('leave a named hook rather than a partial DLQ' for an exhausted PinMissing retry budget) has no corresponding design element anywhere in the document. Add a named, clearly-labeled extension point (or an explicit SCOPE GAP statement deferring it, matching how PIN-01 AC1/AC2 and PIN-03 AC3 are already handled) in the same rework pass.
